Machine Tool Elements and Holding Devices Sectional Committee, PE 02

FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Machine Tool Elements and Holding Devices Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production Engineering Division Council. This Indian Standard was first issued in 1972. This standard has been revised to bring it in line with the current practice. The dimensions of drilling jig have been completely modified and the `dimensions for working space' have been merged into Tables 1 and 2. While preparing this standard considerable assistance has been derived from DIN 6348 : 1971 `Drilling jigs - Quick-clamping', issued by the Deutsches Institut fur Normung (DIN). For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 6440 :1997

Indian Standard

QUICK ACTION DRILLING JIGS SPECIFICATION
( First Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard covers the requirements for quickaction drilling jigs and associated components like base plates and drill plates. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: Title IS No. 210 : 1993 Grey iron castings tion (fourth revision) Specifica7 MATERIAL 7.1 Body of quick-action drilling jigs shall be made from cast iron of grade FG 200 of IS 21C : 1993. 7.2 Base plates and drill plates shall be made from steel conforming to designation Fe 310 (St32) of IS 1570 (Part 1) : 1978. 5 TOLERANCES The dimensional deviations for untoleranced dimensions shall be of medium class in accordance with IS 2102 (Part 1) : 1993. 6 ACCURACY 6.1 When fitted on the drilling jig, the bottom surfaceof drill plateand the clampingsurface of the drill jig shall be ~parallel within 0.025 mm in the entire range of clamping. 6.2 When drill plate is fitted on the drill jig, the guide posts shall be parallel to each other within 0.01 mm. 6.3 The clamping faces of base plates shall be parallel within 0.02 mm for 100 mm.

1570 Schedules for wrought steels : (Part 1) : 1978 Part 1 Steels specified by tensile and/or yield properties (first revision)

General tolerances : Part 1 2102 (Part 1) : 1993 Tolerances for linear and angular 8 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS dimensions without individual tolerances indicated (third 8.1 Components of quick-action drilling jigs, drill plates and base plates shall be free-from cracks, revision) burrs, pits and other defects. All sharp edges shall Hexagon socket head cap screws be removed. 2269 : 1981 (second revision) 8.2 The operation of clamping lever lowers or 3 TYPES raises the drill plate to clamp or unclamp the work. The quick action drilling jigs shall be of two types, The drill plate and base plate shall be adapted to fit the work correctly. namely, Type A and Type B. 4 DIMENSIONS 4.1 Dimensions for quick action drilling jigs, Type A shall be as specified in Table 1 and for Type B shall be as given in Table 2. 4.2 Dimensions for base plates shall be as specified in Table 3. 4.3 Dimensions for drill specified in Table 4. plates shall be as 8.3 The mechanism for lowering or raising the drill plate shall be effective at any height hl. It shall be capable of allowing the clamping lever to be set to the most convenient working position. The difference between the maximum and minimum values of hr shall be the range of adjustment. 8.4 The drill plate is carried on the guide posts and is fitted with jig bushes and, in some cases, with work locators.

Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), B'IS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of~the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Addition..`.
